title: Keenesburg Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Keenesburg wells have a 50-foot median depth, but local records range to 1,030 feet. See yield, water levels, risks and drilling costs.
h1: Keenesburg Colorado Well Depth, Yield and Cost
intro_html:
Buying land around Keenesburg means looking beyond the nearest well record. Permits within 5 miles show a wide range of construction conditions: the median reported well depth is 50 feet, while the middle half runs from 26 to 615 feet and the deepest record reaches 1,030 feet.

Reported production is generally stronger than the depth range suggests. Among the wells with pump-yield records, the median is 13.6 gallons per minute. That is useful local evidence, but it is not a guarantee for an individual parcel. The aquifer name, intended use, nearby well construction and the exact location all matter.

sections.heading: Keenesburg well depths vary sharply across the plains
sections.html:
The Keenesburg records do not describe one consistent drilling depth. Of the wells with reported total depth, 64% are under 100 feet, 2% fall between 100 and 300 feet, 9% are between 300 and 600 feet, and 26% are deeper than 600 feet. The median is 50 feet, but the middle half stretches from 26 to 615 feet.

For a drilling bid, that spread matters more than the median alone. A nearby shallow well may not represent the depth needed on your lot. Denver Basin sedimentary bedrock, alluvial conditions and named Laramie Fox Hills or fractured-bedrock settings can change the planned casing, grout and drilling time. Check several nearby permits before assuming a shallow hole is likely.

sections.heading: What Keenesburg wells produce for a household
sections.html:
Only 316 wells in the records report a pump yield, so the yield statistics are a useful sample rather than a promise for every parcel. The median reported yield is 13.6 gallons per minute, with the middle half between 10.0 and 15.0 gallons per minute. Fifty-two percent of reported yields are between 5 and 15 gallons per minute, and 46% exceed 15 gallons per minute.

No reported well is under 1 gallon per minute, and 2% are between 1 and 5 gallons per minute. That is encouraging for buyers, but low-producing or unsuccessful holes can still occur. Ask for the well test, not just the permit, and confirm that the water right and permit allow the household, stock or irrigation use you need.

sections.heading: Water levels around Keenesburg are not uniform
sections.html:
Only 146 wells report a static water level. Across those records, the median depth to water is 176 feet, with the middle half from 15 to 386 feet. That range is important when estimating pump setting, electrical work and future service access.

The decade medians do not show a simple steadily dropping water table. Reported depth to water was 150 feet in the 1970s, 17 feet in the 1990s, 20 feet in the 2000s, 308 feet in the 2010s and 140 feet in the 2020s. Different locations, aquifers and measurement practices can explain much of that variation. Treat the series as evidence of local variability, not a site-specific forecast.

sections.heading: Keenesburg permit history and active drillers
sections.html:
Colorado DWR records contain 1,572 permitted wells within the mapped area, with 804 recorded as constructed. Permitting increased from 31 permits in each of the 1950s and 1960s to 435 in the 2000s. The records include 218 permits from the 2010s and 227 from the 2020s, with the newest permit year listed as 2025.

The most active driller entry is Authorized (Pe, Pg), associated with 413 records. Glover's Drilling, listed as Glover, Jonathan M., appears on 63, and Holden & Holden, listed as Holden, B L, appears on 50. These are permit-record counts, not endorsements. Confirm current licensing, insurance, availability and the proposed scope directly before hiring.

sections.heading: Keenesburg well drilling cost at local depths
sections.html:
For Denver Basin sedimentary bedrock near Keenesburg, the drilling model uses a typical rate of $50-$70 per foot. At the local median depth of 50 feet, the drilled hole itself models to about $2,500-$3,500. That figure is not the complete water-system price.

A finished well with pump, pressure tank, trenching and electrical is modeled at about $8,500-$15,500 at the median depth. A site needing a much deeper hole can move well beyond that range. Get a written bid that separates drilling, casing and grout, pump equipment, testing, trenching, electrical, access and any permit-related work. The 26-to-615-foot middle-half depth range is a reason to request a site-specific allowance.

sections.heading: Keenesburg risks to check before closing or building
sections.html:
Water quality deserves particular attention. The mapped area within about 10 miles contains 1,253 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, along with 4 historic mine features. There are 0 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites in that search area. Those figures do not determine the quality of a particular well, so test existing water and ask what sampling has been done.

Also investigate low yield, dry-hole risk, water-level variation and the well's construction record. A household well may be exempt, but the permit controls its allowed use; an augmentation plan can matter in an over-appropriated basin. Check septic setbacks, soil, driveway access, building location and separation from possible contamination before finalizing a site plan. Nearby Hudson and Fort Lupton records may provide additional context, but the closest wells are usually more useful.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Keenesburg?
faq.a: The median reported well depth near Keenesburg is 50 feet. The middle half of reported depths runs from 26 to 615 feet, and the deepest record is 1,030 feet. Most are under 100 feet, but 26% are deeper than 600 feet. Nearby permits should guide a site-specific drilling estimate.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Keenesburg?
faq.a: The local drilling model uses $50-$70 per foot. At the 50-foot median depth, the drilled hole is about $2,500-$3,500. A finished system with pump, tank, trenching and electrical is estimated at $8,500-$15,500. A deeper hole, difficult access or added site work can change the bid.

faq.q: How much water do wells produce in Keenesburg?
faq.a: Among 316 wells with reported pump yields, the median is 13.6 gallons per minute. The middle half produces 10.0-15.0 gallons per minute. No reported well is under 1 gallon per minute, but that sample does not guarantee a result on an untested parcel. Request the actual well test and permit use.

faq.q: Is well water safe in Keenesburg?
faq.a: The records map 1,253 PFAS sampling or contamination sites within about 10 miles, plus 4 historic mine features. That does not prove a specific well is unsafe, and there are 0 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites in the area. Test existing water and arrange quality testing before buying or occupying a property.

faq.q: Is the water table dropping near Keenesburg?
faq.a: The reported decade medians do not show a steady decline. Depth to water was 150 feet in the 1970s, 17 feet in the 1990s, 20 feet in the 2000s, 308 feet in the 2010s and 140 feet in the 2020s. Because only 146 wells report static levels, use nearby measurements rather than the series alone.
